$comment: The defended repository inventory — one machine-readable declaration of every
Dagger module and every active consumer-facing surface in this repository.
Consumed by scripts/repo_surface.py (the checker), scripts/_pin_targets.py
(release pin rewriting + CI pin guard) and scripts/bump-version.py. Nothing may
keep a competing hand-maintained list: drift between the bumper's file set and
the guard's file set is what let .github/workflows/ freeze at v0.2.0 and let a
workflow ship calling `run-archive` against a composite that no longer had it.
Rules the checker enforces (scripts/check-repo-surface.py):
- every path declared here must exist; a missing path is an ERROR, never a skip
- `find src -name dagger.json` and `modules` agree exactly, both directions
- schema_synced_modules / contract_modules are subsets of modules and their
schema.go / contract.json actually exist
- every markdown file under discovery.markdown_roots is declared or sits under
an explicit historical_exclusions prefix — nothing active stays unscanned
- every context-and-oss/cicd version pin in an active surface agrees on one version
- every `dagger -m <this repo's module> call <cmd>` resolves to an exported
method in that module's Go source
- every local markdown link in an active surface resolves to a real path
schema_modules$comment: Modules carrying a copy of src/internal/evidence/schema.go. Dagger modules are
isolated (one go.mod each) so the canonical types are shared by file copy.
The composites and src/cross-cutting/{contract,report,pages} are absent because
they read evidence through their dependencies and hold no schema copy — the
Makefile previously listed four of them and hid the mismatch behind an
schema_synced_modules$comment: Subset of schema_modules whose schema.go is regenerated by
scripts/sync-schema.py (make sync-schema). src/risk is deliberately absent: it
keeps the canonical exported shape because risk/opa.go references ValidSeverity
synced_files$comment: Groups of files that must be byte-identical. Dagger modules are isolated —
no module can import another's Go package — so a helper two modules both
need is shared by file copy, the same way schema.go is. schema.go has a
generator (make sync-schema); these do not, so the equality is asserted
here instead of assumed. A copy nothing asserts drifts for exactly as long
as nothing tests the pair together: .slnx went missing from two of
markers.go's three copies that way, and readback.go said "keep them
byte-identical" in a comment nothing read.
A pair belongs here when one copy's drift would change a verdict the other
module's evidence cannot see: a drifted feedTransportOK puts a feed token on
a cleartext wire from one module and refuses it from the other, and nothing
in the passing module's evidence would say so.
A group may set "may_differ_by": "module-sdk-import", the one declared
difference: each copy's import of its own module's generated SDK, read from
the go.mod beside it, is set aside before comparing. A helper that takes a
*dagger.File cannot otherwise be shared at all, since every module imports
its SDK as "<module path>/internal/dagger". Nothing else is normalised.

synced_files.reason: Git diff header parser: which files a change touched, quoted, binary, mode-only and renamed paths included, and the refusal of a diff without a/ and b/ prefixes. intent scopes its artifacts to it; risk scopes its change-scoped infrastructure scan to it. The two carried a parser each, wrong in different ways, and both errors read as a change that touched nothing.
The test table for the shared diff header parser, kept beside each copy so either module's unit suite proves the parser it compiles.

NuGet feed transport check, feed-URL comparison and NuGet.Config rendering. quality restores for its .NET lint and test legs; security restores for the lockfile-free dependency-graph fallback (src/security/dotnetrestore.go).

Language marker-file list, the find(1) predicate generated from it and the suffix classification. quality detects the languages its lint and test legs run; build infers the toolchain language for BuildArchive (src/build/archive.go). src/internal/detect/detect.go carries the same suffixes in an fs.FS walker and is kept in step by hand.

gatedPassed, the one rule that keeps `--fail-on NONE` from suppressing a non-run. Each file holds that function alone; module-specific helpers live in src/quality/legfold.go and src/risk/validatereport.go so an addition to one copy cannot break the equality.

readbackError and readbackCount: the errors[] wording for a leg output cicd could not read back out of the container, and the rule that an unreadable or non-numeric sentinel is never a count of zero. quality and security both collect every tool's output this way.

The .NET SDK band rule: what a tree asks for (global.json sdk.version, else the highest literal TargetFramework) and which pinned band serves it. quality lints and tests in that band; security restores the dependency graph in it. security used to carry a trimmed copy that agreed with quality's only by inspection, and a module that resolved the same tree to a different band would attribute its verdict to an SDK the other never ran.

The audit tail every composite ends in: Wrap, the Teams delivery as evidence, Wrap again (which is what performs the lazy notification), then the PR comment. commit, precommit and dast each carried a hand-kept copy, and a copy that drops the second Wrap stops sending cards while every run still reports success. The copies import their own module's SDK, so that one line is the declared difference.

generated_files$comment: Files generated from a canonical implementation by a script here, and
regenerated by check-surface to prove they still match it. Distinct from
synced_files, and the distinction is the drift each one can see.
synced_files compares copies against each other, which is blind to the
failure that actually happens: edit the canonical file, forget every copy,
and the copies stay byte-identical while disagreeing with the code they are
copies of — the comparison passes and reports nothing. Measured on this
very change: appending a line to src/internal/detect/toolchain.go left both
module copies with the identical md5, so a copy-vs-copy check saw a clean
tree while the generator check flagged both. That is .slnx again with the
comparison pointed at the wrong pair.
So a group belongs here rather than in synced_files whenever the copies can
be produced mechanically. The generator is the declaration of what the copy
is allowed to differ by; anything else is drift.

generated_files.reason: the ADR-004 toolchain resolver. Dagger modules are isolated, so quality and build carry generated copies of the canonical implementation; the generator inlines the Language type and rewrites the package clause and changes nothing else.
Bounded independent check and test-leg scheduling; default remains sequential.

$comment: Files a consumer, contributor or auditor reads as a current statement about
how this repository behaves. Every group is checked for missing paths, pin
coherence, Dagger command existence and local link resolution.
Which active surfaces scripts/bump-version.py rewrites, split by push
credential. GitHub refuses to let the default GITHUB_TOKEN push changes to
.github/workflows/ — only a credential carrying the `workflow` scope can — so
the release runs that pass separately (--scope workflows).
These are group NAMES from active_surfaces, not a second file list. Pin
coherence is checked across every active surface regardless of group, so a
surface that is not rewritten here still cannot silently lag.
A composite gains a parameter in Go and the starter surfaces do not follow.
Nothing notices: the composite keeps its default, every pipeline stays green,
and the feature exists for whoever calls the module by hand and for nobody
else. --license-gate, --license-allow and --license-exclude reached
precommit.yml and commit.yml never at all, so a consumer on the commit lane
read licence findings it had no way to act on.
surface_groups names the active_surfaces groups a consumer configures. This
repository's own internal_workflows are out of scope on purpose: they are one
team's pinned choices, not a product surface, and grading them would bury the
real gaps under thirty excuses per file.
Every entry under `unreachable` says why that parameter is legitimately out
of reach from those surfaces, in the same spirit as
workflow_actions.third_party_allowed. A stale entry is itself a problem: once
a parameter is forwarded, the excuse has to go, or this list becomes a
second, quieter place where a knob can be unreachable.

unreachable.reason: Language selection defaults to marker-file auto-detection, which is the documented behaviour. Routing it through an ADO pipeline variable is refused outright: an undefined ADO macro arrives as its own literal text and quality.Check then fails the run naming that text as an unknown language. These templates therefore document the flag in prose and tell the reader to add --include to the call line by hand, which is the only form that cannot be silently emptied.

The fan-out runs one job per application, each with its own source root and its own languages. A single --include list would apply to every application at once, which is the wrong shape; per-app language selection would belong in the caller's matrix, and auto-detection already gives it.

The pre-commit lane runs the module's default ruleset, and both templates carry a prose block telling the reader which --sast-rulesets values to add to the call line to curate it. Never routed through a variable: an empty ruleset is a Semgrep false pass (src/security/CLAUDE.md), and an ADO variable is exactly how one arrives empty.

The absolute coverage percentage gate. It defaults to 0 (off), and a single threshold reachable from a starter surface either blocks every repository that adopts cicd on day one or is set low enough to mean nothing. It belongs with the ratchet, which measures a repository against its own prior run; the two are exposed together or not at all.
The small-language escape hatch for min-coverage. It qualifies a threshold that is itself unreachable from these surfaces, so on its own it changes nothing.

The witnessed BYO test command. The ADO starters run cicd's own per-language test legs; a team on ADO that owns test execution calls the module directly, where the command, its coverage report path and its toolchain can be set together. The monorepo fan-out takes the per-app --test-legs form instead, because one command cannot describe several applications.

The polyglot form of --test-cmd, a JSON array of per-language legs. Same reason as --test-cmd on these surfaces, and an ADO pipeline variable is a poor home for a JSON document that must survive macro expansion before bash sees it.

Names the report the BYO test command writes. The ADO precommit starters use native runners rather than test-cmd. The monorepo workflow uses per-app test-legs with per-leg coveragePath instead of a run-wide path.

The coverage ratchet's prior evidence document. cicd stores no baseline, so the caller has to fetch one and stage it in the workspace before the composite runs; no starter surface does that today, and a ratchet with no baseline fails open. Exposing the file path before there is a way to produce the file would hand a consumer a gate that silently never runs.
The allowed coverage drop before the ratchet trips. It qualifies a ratchet that cannot run from these surfaces because --baseline is unreachable.
Chooses whether a tripped ratchet fails or warns. Same reason as --tolerance: there is no reachable ratchet for it to govern.
ADR-004 level 1, the explicit toolchain override, applies to the witnessed BYO test command, which neither template exposes. An image with no consumer command to run in it changes nothing.

It defaults to true and the only value a consumer could set is false, which stops the scan reading source headers and LICENSE files. In ecosystems whose manifests carry no licence field, Go among them, that is the difference between findings and none, reported as a clean result. A knob whose single effect is to make a scan quietly read less is not one this repository puts on a starter surface.

Live secret verification sends candidate credentials found in the image to the issuing provider to ask whether they still work. That is an outbound call from a consumer's pipeline to a third party carrying the consumer's own secrets, so it stays a deliberate direct invocation rather than a pipeline input someone can flip without reading what it does.

Names which application inside a monorepo this run covers, and appears in the evidence artifact name so several runs do not collide. A single-application pipeline has exactly one, so the parameter could only be set wrong; .github/workflows/commit-monorepo.yml is the surface that owns it.

Scopes a monorepo run to one application's directories. A single-application pipeline scans its whole checkout by definition, and narrowing scope must be named where it is decided, which is the fan-out caller's matrix.

Per-language lint legs declared as JSON, the counterpart of --test-legs. Only the monorepo surface exposes it, because its callers already write a per-application JSON matrix; a single-application consumer gets marker-file auto-detection, the documented default.

The per-application job is already scoped by --source-paths, and the fan-out caller decides which applications run at all. A repository-wide diff would not narrow anything the matrix has not narrowed first.

One Dockerfile path cannot describe several applications. Each per-application job builds from its own source root with the module default, and a per-app override belongs in the caller's matrix if anyone asks for one.
Same as --dockerfile: a single OCI platform for a fan-out over several applications is the wrong shape, and linux/amd64 is the module default every application in the fan-out builds for today.
The per-application job produces evidence and uploads it; notification happens once in the aggregating caller. Wiring the webhook in here would post one Teams card per application in the fan-out.

The change-intent gate's artifact patterns. The gate is opt-in, and its built-in globs cover the artifact kinds this repository documents; a team with its own artifact naming calls the module directly rather than through a starter, which is also where it can read what the patterns are matched against.

Dependabot is a GitHub feature. On Azure DevOps there is no dependabot[bot] actor for the caller to verify, and this flag must only ever be set by a caller that has verified the actor itself, so exposing it here would offer nothing but a way to get it wrong.

The monorepo fan-out calls the commit composite in application mode (--app-id), and that path runs no vulnerability leg at all: ScanSource is invoked code-only and ScanArchive artifact-only, so Trivy never produces a row there to accept. Forwarding the flag would warn VULN ACCEPTANCE UNUSED on every application job, which trains readers to ignore the one line that says an acceptance has gone stale. The lane's dependency findings come from the whole-repository commit.yml, which exposes vuln-accept.
Application mode declares lint/test legs explicitly and does not discover Node projects. The repository discovery budget is rejected in app mode.

Low-level Dagger container handoff for consumer-owned orchestration. Workflow starters do not receive a prepared Container from another module call; commit workflows construct it from prepare-cmd instead. Precommit forwards stage-2 context options for Dagger callers.

unreadable_sites.reason: The local pre-push helper resolves its module into a shell variable so it can fall back from the pinned remote reference to a checked-out ./src/composites/precommit. This check reads literal module references only, so it grades no parameter here. It is a developer convenience running the same composite .github/workflows/precommit.yml runs, and that workflow is the surface a consumer configures.

$comment: A flag that switches on an optional outbound channel must be passed only
when its value exists. Passing it unconditionally does not fail — it
succeeds quietly against nothing: a secret the repository never defines
still arrives at the composite as a non-nil, empty Secret under GitHub
Actions `secrets: inherit`, and an undefined Azure DevOps variable arrives
as its own literal text `$(NAME)`. cicd POSTed a Teams card to the empty
string on every run of every repository that had not set Teams up, wrote
`unsupported protocol scheme ""` into a log nobody reads, and reported
success. dast.yml carried the guard from the start; commit.yml,
precommit.yml and all four Azure DevOps templates drifted without it.
The module now tells the three states apart in evidence, so an unguarded
flag no longer lies. It is still wrong: it puts a NOT CONFIGURED warning
into the pull request comment of every consumer who never asked for the
channel, and a disclosure on every run is noise. The guard is what keeps
the leg from running at all.
Each entry names the flag, the value form it is passed as, and the reason.
A guarded occurrence appends to a shell array inside a conditional that
names the same variable; the conditional is required, because an
unconditional `extra+=(--flag env:NAME)` is the same defect one line over.
--diff is the same shape with the opposite failure. A workflow that could
not compute the change diff used to write an empty file and pass it, and
the intent gate read the empty diff as a change that touched nothing in
scope and audited the whole tree instead, passing a pull request that
carried no artifact. A diff that could not be computed now fails the step;
a build with nothing to diff passes no --diff at all, so the guard is what
separates 'no scope asked for' from 'scope asked for and lost'. See
specs/a-diff-the-workflow-could-not-compute-is-not-an-empty-diff.md.

flags.reason: A Teams incoming webhook is opt-in. Unset, it reaches the composite as an empty Secret (GitHub) or the literal $(TEAMS_WEBHOOK) (Azure DevOps), and notify then reports a channel nobody configured on every run.

The change diff scopes the intent gate. A diff that was never computed must not reach the composite as an empty file, which intent reads as a change touching nothing and answers with a whole-tree audit; it is passed only when the workflow wrote a non-empty diff.

$comment: Which action owners a declared workflow may use. This repository's Actions
policy is `selected`, permitting GitHub-owned and verified-creator actions
with no extra patterns. A disallowed action does not fail its step — GitHub
refuses the run at startup, so no job is created and no check run is
published: the pipeline vanishes from the PR check list instead of turning
red. ci.yml (golangci/golangci-lint-action) and cd.yml (taiki-e/install-
action) sat dead that way from 2026-07-30 to 2026-08-03 while PRs merged on
a check list that never mentioned them.
So the trust set is declared here and checked by scripts/check-repo-surface.py
rather than trusted to fail loudly at run time. Adding a third-party action
requires an explicit third_party_allowed entry with a reason, which forces
whoever adds it to confirm the policy actually permits it. Local actions
(`uses: ./...`) are always allowed by GitHub and need no declaration — that
is why the pinned git-cliff install lives in .github/actions/.
workflow_groups names groups from active_surfaces, not a second file list.
local_actions is in scope too: a composite action can itself `uses:` another
action, and a third-party one there kills startup exactly the same way.
check-workflow-pins.py is the CI-blocking gate: ci.yml runs it on every push
and cd.yml runs it inside the release commit's bump_and_validate step. Brief
01 widened pin-coherence scanning to every active surface (scripts/check-
repo-surface.py) and parked the drift it surfaced here — nine files that were
never in the old hand-maintained TARGETS list, so nothing ever bumped them
past v1.0.0 — so the blocking gate stayed green for unrelated work.
That list is now EMPTY and must stay empty. The v1.8.0 release bump rewrote
all nine pins (they are inventory-derived targets now), and a follow-up change repaired
the removed-command and broken-link drift alongside it, so the two checkers
agree on pin coherence again: check-repo-surface.py is green on the live tree
and is wired into ci.yml next to the blocking gate.
tolerate_pending stays a supported flag so a future widening can be landed
with an explicit, reasoned, self-expiring exception rather than a silent
skip — but an exception is a debt, not a resting state. Every entry is
checked against the live tree: an entry whose pin no longer lags is refused
(check_pending_pin_repairs), so the list cannot outlive the drift it excuses.
Delete an entry in the same change that repairs its pin.

historical_exclusions.reason: Shape/brief planning material for delivered and in-flight work, kept for provenance. Historical by construction: a spec records the intent at authoring time, not current behaviour, and is never rewritten to match today's surface.

$comment: Where the checker looks for material that should have been declared.
module_root drives dagger.json discovery. markdown_roots drive the
undeclared-active-document check; anything under a historical_exclusions
prefix is skipped, everything else must appear in active_surfaces.
Roots deliberately absent (not repository surfaces, so nothing to exclude):
.claude/  agent tooling configuration
testdata/ language fixture apps consumed by tests
.capsules/ decision records, historical by construction
